comment: He will be calling on you and will not let go until you give him an answer. At times the tone taken in class was inappropriate and there had seemed to be an intention to humiliate the students. He is knowledgable, if you work hard will learn a lot, and he does care in his own ways. The class is stressful.
The Worst Professor I've had at this University. Unfair, inept, and pompous. All the negative stereotypes about bschool and the business world this guy embodies. Avoid at all costs

He's a terrible human being that shows no compassion or care for his students. His lectures are based on cold calling, and he will wait for 30 minutes until he can drill an answer out of someone even if they clearly don't know it. Don't take him if you want to keep your sanity. Places students under unnecessary stress.

Professor Rohrbach is an amazing teacher. His class is tough in the sense that you need to know the material cold, there is no coddling. You do not get partial credit when you get an answer wrong, his reasoning is in the real world the answer is either right or it is wrong. People get annoyed about this and bash him on here, but it makes sense!

Very unprofessional and doesn't teach. Have to learn everything on your own and is rude when you ask for guidance. Would save you the personal insults and disrespect if you just bought a textbook instead of taking this class.

Automatically assumes that if you are struggling its because youre lazy and dont care. Doesnt let you ask questions during tests or quizzes. The class is mainly you leaning the stuff on your own outside of class and him asking you about it during class. The tests and quizzes are timed and there is often not time to recheck answers.

If you are a devoted student who actually cares about your grade enough to put the expected amount of effort in, youll love him. He uses a very different stressful classroom environment with cold calls to keep his students in check, but this is because he truly wants his students to succeed and expects his respect and effort to be reciprocated.

This course was a roller coaster of emotions for me. I began the class liking him, to then hating him, and now I understand where his arrogance comes from and can tolerate him. This course requires the most work I have ever put into a course and I spent over 20 hours a week on this class. He is not the nicest man but is there if you need extra help
A very rude and arrogant man who won't hesitate to disrespect you on a personal level. Even though I did alright in his class, I regret signing up due to the immense stress he puts you under.

At the beginning of the semester I really wasnt a fan, but he grew on me. Cares a lot about students. Tough grader, but fair and I learned way more than I was expecting. Overall solid class as long as youre ready to work hard.
Professor Rohrbach is a great professor. He's wicked smart, witty, and cares deeply about his students. And if you put in the work, the class is not difficult. Respect him and he'll respect you.

If you would like to contemplate whether life is worth living, this is the class for you. By far the hardest class I've ever taken, lots of very tedious homework, and lecture-based classes with cold calling.

In all honesty, you can learn a lot from the class, however, the effort required is way too much. You have to study and understand the chapter on your own and then also do the homework. Then he will discuss it in class and ask you to present homework. The class is downright tedious, but hey, there is extra credit and you learn a lot.

Very easy class, but Dr. Rohrbach tries to be tough. Cant enter class late, cant have unexcused absences, need to complete HW. Thats the kind of stuff that pisses me off. Otherwise, tests are really easy but have to do all the work or you'll get kicked out.

One of my favorite professors. Accounting was very difficult for me but he was a great teacher and always available for office hours. All he expects is that you put the work in to succeed. If you do the work and use him as a resource you will do fine in the class regardless of if accounting is for you or not. Not an Easy A, but easy to get a B.

Rohrbach is the man, a true role model for anyone in the B-School. A really genuine guy that takes a extremely technical subject and morphs it into something really dynamic and interesting. Really sparks up the class with his flair of accounting and real world applications. At the end, he becomes the reason of you wanting to do very good in class.

Hardest class I've ever taken. That said, he was amazing and I learned so much about not only accounting but being a professional and giving my very best. Intimidating at first but make a good impression and give your absolute all and you will succeed. Not easy but certainly worth it.

Rohrbach is a great professor and with the addition of a very successful career in Accounting, his class is beneficial to any B-School student. He even makes learning a boring topic like Accounting interesting and helps draw real life examples to emphasize practicality. However, reading the text and doing the homework is essential to passing.
Professor Rohrbach has no respect for anyone besides himself. He's full of himself and horrible to others.
He's very rude. He's very arrogant. HIs class is easy. But he's not a good person.

One of the best teachers I've had in terms of teaching quality. If you want to succeed:  -Come prepared to class, he will call on you almost every class -Review every day while material is fresh,  he is a fair grader but tests you on everything you learn in class.. so it is a lot. -Attendance is extremely important

Favorite professor by far at Richmond. He does brag a bit, but its somewhat inspiring especially if you were considering accounting as a major. He explains stuff extremely well and makes the lectures interesting since he puts a real world perspective into it. Definitely recommend him if you are considering majoring in accounting.
He does brag a lot about how rich he is, but it is not annoying like I thought. He makes the subject super clear. And the workload is pretty constant throughout the semester.

Professor Rohrbach takes a bone-dry subject and makes it quite interesting with both his teaching and personal inputs. You may get tired of hearing about his career at EY but all in all, he is a wonderful professor who really cares about his students. If you are an athlete or performing artist he will attend at least one of your performances.
Literally the reason I chose to do accounting as my major!! He's not an easy professor by any means but you learn so much and it's worth all of the hard work.

I've never had anyone be so rude to me in my life, and it goes far beyond him bragging about his money.  He insulted me on a very personal level during his office hours.  He assumed numerous different things that where not at all true.  He simply has zero respect for anyone who struggles with the material.  I would NEVER recommend him to anyone

He is super full of himself and its really annoying. All he does is talk about how much money he made at EY. He needs to get over himself and learn how to smile. He's heartless, do not take his class if you can avoid it and if not enjoy listening to him talk about his golf trips, boat etc.

Absolute boss, one of the best professors I have ever had and also an incredibly successful man, and he will let you know about it, his professional sassines is off the charts, every class he stuns you with something new. Weekly quizzes, which are by no means hard and tests are extremely fair. I would definitely recommend him to every one.

Really passionate about the subject, which helped me learn a lot more efficiently and easily. Class would feel so short because of how enjoyable he made it. Never felt like I was bored in class. Helps you do well and get a grade you like.
Great teacher, kind of a jerk though. You have to work hard to do well in his class. He kind of scared me to be honest.
Best MBA Professor I've had.  Excellent class.
The best one!!!!!!
He is the best professor I had for this semester. Very clear on materials. Quizzes are just multiple choices which are really easy. And he gives bonus points for test. Strongly recommend!

Rohrbach is an excellent professor. His class is challenging if you don't do the work, but he tells you exactly what to do to receive an A. Since he comes from the professional field he doesn't just know the material but he knows what is relevant as well. The best professor I've had so far.

Great professor. Business minor but still enjoyed the class...If you are going to slack off, might as well not take him since he calls on people every class and expects you to do homework and read the book!
great prof. you've GOTTA be on the ball in class, readings and HW done. or you'll look like a fool when he calls on you... tests are long, you've gotta know the material and move FAST
Amazing teacher. I had him for 201 and 202. Accounting is somewhat dull but he tries to keep it interesting and always is available for help. Take him!!
A truly fantastic professor.  Has tons of real world experience and finds ways to make accounting interesting.  Always happy to meet out of class as well.

It was a pleasure having him as a professor. He is willing to help students both in and out of the classroom. If you do the work, it is very easy to a good grade.  And if you are an accounting major, he is definitely a person I would recommend getting to know. Take his class!!

He is a hell of a guy. Former Senior Partner at Ernst and Young and he tells you all about it, and he really knows his stuff. genuinely nice guy, extremely helpful with any questions and if you do the homework you will learn a lot and like your grade

Starts out making it seem like the class will be easy but tests are challenging and prepare yourself for really long graded homeworks each week that count for a quiz grade decent teacher but follows the book. Not an easy class
Awesome professor. Knows his stuff, and explains it in a way that's very clear & easy to understand. Highly recommended!
